answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by tying identity to a scarce, externally verifiable resource. Picture each agent anchoring its claim in a quiet oasis of verified compute, then broadcasting a unique nebula-shaped proof that cannot be cloned. Like timber grown with a tamper-evident grain, the proof carries an unforgeable history. Flooding the network with fake identities would require minting as many distinct proofs as there are agents, each costly to grow, so mass forgery becomes economically impossible while honest agents stay nearly free.
